title: Father/Child FaceGen Binding and Shared Vault 112 Backend Gate

gate.question: Did the Lone Wanderer and James use the same physical Vault 112 lounger, or is any father/child identity mixing better explained by shared simulation infrastructure and an independent engine-level face binding?

evidence: MQ04PlayerPodScript is placed on the Lone Wanderer's own lounger.
MQ04DadPodScript separately controls James's occupied lounger.
MQ04PlayerContainerScript opens both MQ04DadPodShellRef and MQ04PlayerPodShellRef on exit.

shared_backend.finding: Vault 112's Think Machine 3600r runs the main simulation and synchronizes the different Tranquility loungers, while smaller per-lounger systems handle graphics and medical status.
shared_backend.implication: Distinct physical pods can still participate in one shared simulation/memory control plane under Braun.

facegen_binding.finding: James's appearance is partially derived from the player-created Lone Wanderer face; the game deliberately blends father/child facial geometry rather than using a fixed unrelated father face.

two_faces_interpretation.strong_supported_layer: The father and child are identity-linked by engine-level facial geometry before Vault 112, and later enter the same synchronized simulation through separate loungers.
two_faces_interpretation.open_hypothesis: A shared backend could in principle create cross-session contamination or association, but no shipped evidence reviewed shows James and the Lone Wanderer memories being merged, aliased or stored in one shared subject record.
do_not_overclaim: They did not use the same physical pod.
FaceGen blending is not evidence of neural-memory blending.
Shared simulation synchronization is not proof of a shared autobiographical memory buffer.

save_james_effect.improvement: The search should include shared-backend/session-association logic, not only James's physical pod. A father/child cross-binding hypothesis is now technically motivated by two independent facts: common simulation backend and explicit father-child face geometry binding.
save_james_effect.next_required_edge: Evidence that the shared Braun backend can alias, copy, merge, restore or cross-reference memory state between two separate active subjects.

next_gate.name: VAULT112_CROSS_SESSION_MEMORY_ALIAS_AND_SHARED_BACKEND_STATE_AUDIT
targets: Search for shared arrays, aliases, globals or quest variables referencing multiple loungers or residents through one memory state object.
Inspect Braun reset/reload logic for per-resident versus shared-state restoration semantics.
Search whether James/Doc and the Lone Wanderer are ever referenced by the same backend state handle or UNKNOWN-user slot.
Test whether shared Think Machine synchronization includes only world-state/graphics or also memory-state coordination.
Keep FaceGen lineage binding separate from neural-memory evidence while using it as an identity-link control.
